chapters.name: Matter in Our Surroundings
subtopics: States of Matter: Solid, Liquid, Gas
Change of State: Melting, Freezing, Evaporation, Condensation, Sublimation
key_concepts: Matter is anything that has mass and occupies space
Particles of matter are continuously moving
Particles of matter have space between them
Particles of matter attract each other

chapters.name: Is Matter Around Us Pure?
key_concepts: Mixture contains two or more substances physically combined
Compound contains two or more substances chemically combined
Physical change does not produce new substance
deleted_topics: Separation of Components of a Mixture (removed from 2025-26)

chapters.name: Atoms and Molecules
key_concepts: Atom is the smallest particle of an element
Molecule is a group of two or more atoms
Ion is an atom or molecule with a charge
Chemical formula represents composition of a compound
Molecular mass is sum of atomic masses
Mole concept relates mass to number of particles
formulas: Molecular mass = sum of atomic masses of all atoms

chapters.name: Structure of the Atom
subtopics: How are Electrons Distributed in Different Orbits?
key_concepts: Thomson: atom is positive sphere with electrons embedded
Rutherford: atom has dense nucleus with electrons orbiting
Bohr: electrons revolve in fixed orbits/shells
Valency is combining capacity of an atom
Isotopes: same atomic number, different mass number
Isobars: same mass number, different atomic number
formulas: Mass Number (A) = Number of protons + Number of neutrons

chapters.name: The Fundamental Unit of Life
subtopics: What are Living Organisms Made Up of?
What is a Cell Made Up of?
How do Substances Move in and out of the Cell?
key_concepts: Cell is the basic structural and functional unit of life
Cell wall provides shape and protection (plants)
Osmosis: movement of water through semipermeable membrane

chapters.name: Tissues
subtopics: Animal Tissues: Epithelial, Connective, Muscular, Nervous
Structure and Functions of Each Tissue Type
key_concepts: Tissue is a group of cells with similar structure and function
Permanent tissue: cells that have stopped dividing
Simple permanent tissue: Parenchyma, Collenchyma, Sclerenchyma
Complex permanent tissue: Xylem and Phloem

chapters.name: Motion
subtopics: Describing Motion: Distance, Displacement, Speed, Velocity
Measuring the Rate of Motion: Speed and Velocity
Rate of Change of Velocity: Acceleration
Graphical Representation of Motion: Distance-Time and Velocity-Time Graphs
Equations of Motion by Graphical Method
key_concepts: Displacement is shortest distance between two points (vector)
Uniform motion: constant speed in straight line
Velocity-time graph: slope = acceleration, area = displacement
Equations of motion: v = u + at, s = ut + ½at², v² = u² + 2as
Uniform circular motion: speed constant, direction changes
formulas: Average speed = total distance / total time
Average velocity = total displacement / total time

chapters.name: Force and Laws of Motion
key_concepts: Force is a push or pull that changes state of motion
Balanced forces: net force is zero, no change in motion
Unbalanced forces: net force is not zero, causes acceleration
First Law: object remains at rest or in uniform motion unless acted upon by unbalanced force
Inertia: tendency of body to resist change in state
Second Law: F = ma (force equals mass times acceleration)
Third Law: every action has equal and opposite reaction
Conservation of Momentum: total momentum before = total momentum after
formulas: Impulse = Force × time = change in momentum
m₁u₁ + m₂u₂ = m₁v₁ + m₂v₂ (conservation of momentum)

chapters.name: Gravitation
key_concepts: Every object attracts every other object with gravitational force
Gravity is gravitational force of Earth on objects near its surface
Mass is constant; weight varies with gravity
Free fall: object falling under gravity alone
Thrust: perpendicular force on a surface
Buoyant force: upward force on immersed object
Archimedes' Principle: buoyant force = weight of displaced fluid
Relative density = density of substance / density of water
formulas: Relative Density = Density of substance / Density of water

chapters.name: Work and Energy
key_concepts: Work done when force moves an object: W = Fs cos θ
Work is scalar quantity, unit: Joule (J)
Kinetic Energy: energy of motion, KE = ½mv²
Potential Energy: stored energy due to position
Energy can neither be created nor destroyed, only transformed
Power: rate of doing work, P = W/t

chapters.name: Sound
subtopics: Speed of Sound in Different Media
key_concepts: Sound is produced by vibration of objects
Sound needs medium to travel (solid, liquid, gas)
Characteristics: amplitude, frequency, time period, wavelength
Speed of sound: solid > liquid > gas
formulas: Speed of sound in air ≈ 344 m/s at 22°C

chapters.name: Improvement in Food Resources
subtopics: Improvement in Food Resources from Animals
key_concepts: Crop production improvement: irrigation, fertilizers, protection
Crop protection management: weeds, pests, diseases
Manure and fertilizers improve soil fertility
Animal husbandry: cattle farming, poultry farming
